comments.content:
@pavlovcik 
There is the supabase [diff tool](https://supabase.com/docs/reference/cli/supabase-db-diff) which can create "diff" migrations between DB schemas.
So I took your local DB dump (which you DMed me) and created this [migration script](https://github.com/rndquu/bounty-bot/blob/f09ba3a1363c01417fc236b1242a7c32f96603b2/supabase/migrations/20231019155701_refactor_general.sql).
Here is how I generated it:
1. Start supabase locally (migrations are applied automatically on start)
```
yarn supabase start
```
2. Create a remote supabase project at https://supabase.com/dashboard/projects
3. Connect to a remote DB (at supabase) with [pgAdmin](https://www.pgadmin.org/)
4. Restore DB from a sql dump of the updated DB schema. Select the `public` schema in `pgAdmin`, open `psql` tool from `pgAdmin` and run sql dump script via `\i  /Users/username/Downloads/updated_schema.sql`.
5. Link a remote project
```
yarn supabase link -p PASSWORD --project-ref PROJECT_REF
``` 
6. Run the diff tool between a local DB (without changes) and a remote DB from supabase (with updated schema)
```
yarn supabase db diff --linked -f refactor_general
```
7. Apply newly generate "diff" migration
```
yarn supabase db reset
```
This "diff" migration should be generated and debugged when you're finished with the current refactor. So when you're finished you could share a sql dump of your final DB schema and I would generate and debug the "diff" migration.
Tomorrow I will check [supabase triggers](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/postgres/triggers) and how we can use them to populate the `locations` (i.e. metadata) table.

@pavlovcik Regarding the `locations` and metadata. This is how the schema looks like right now: Each table has the `location_id` field which is a reference to the `location` entity which is basically some fields from the github event that caused the row to be inserted in the original table. We have 3 DB operations which cause an update: 1. create 2. update 3. delete The issue with the current schema is that it reflects only `create` DB operations. For example, when user registers a new wallet then a new corresponding `location` entity is created and `wallet.location_id` is populated. But when a user updates a wallet then it is not clear what we should do with the `wallet.location_id` field, rewrite it or keep the old value. It is weird, but supabase does not support insertions with relations which leaves us with 3 options: 1. Use postgres [RPC calls](https://supabase.com/docs/reference/javascript/rpc). So for each model update we should write a separate RPC method which is really hard to a maintain. 2. Use postgres [triggers](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/postgres/triggers). This approach adds redundancy because for each table we should add a new virtual field `location` which we should keep in mind on all create/update/delete operations (ex: `await supabase.from("wallets").upsert({...walletObj, ...locationObj}`) 3. Use 2 separate API calls The original issue sounds like "we should save github event metadata to all DB create/update/delete operations". We could do it this way: 1. Remove `location_id` from all of the tables 2. Add `uuid` field to all of the tables 3. Modify the `locations` table to have the following fields: `id serial`, `entity_uuid uuid`, `operation text`, `github_event jsonb` 4. Hook into the original `supabase client SDK` to send a 2nd API call to the `locations` table on each create/update/delete operation ## Example (user registers a new wallet): ### wallet | uuid | address | | ------------- | ------------- | | 1111-2222 | 0x01 | ### locations | id | entity_uuid | operation | github_event | | ------------- | ------------- | --- | --- | | 1 | 1111-2222 | create | `{node_id:1,node_html:"https://github.com",issue_id:3,etc...}` | ## Example (user updates a wallet): ### wallet | uuid | address | | ------------- | ------------- | | 1111-2222 | 0x02 | ### locations | id | entity_uuid | operation | github_event | | ------------- | ------------- | --- | --- | | 1 | 1111-2222 | create | `{node_id:1,node_html:"https://github.com",issue_id:3,etc...}` | | 2 | 1111-2222 | update | `{node_id:2,node_html:"https://github.com",issue_id:3,etc...}` | Overall this issue of tracking corresponding metadata (i.e. github event context object) can be safely moved to a separate issue in order not to blow the current PR.
We can start simple for now and then implement some retry strategy for failed metadata updates.
